turns.content: Hello, I'm your doctor today. What brings you in today?

I’m here because I have lower chest pain on the right side—it feels like a knife-stab pain. It started pretty fast, about 5/10 in speed, and it’s been around 7/10 intensity, with right breast pain too. I also feel significant shortness of breath, palpitations, and I’ve had some new tired/vague discomfort and muscle aches since a recent viral infection, plus I get worse when I’m lying down (orthopnea).

I’m sorry you’re dealing with this. **One question at a time**:

**1) When did the chest pain start (how many hours ago), and is it worse with deep breathing or coughing (pleuritic)?**
It started about a few hours ago—around 3 to 4 hours. It feels worse when I take a deep breath, so I think it is kind of pleuritic, and I haven’t noticed much with coughing.
Thanks. **2) Do you have any leg symptoms—pain/swelling in one calf, or recent long travel/immobility?**
No, I don’t have any leg pain or swelling in one calf. And I haven’t had any recent long travel or been immobile.
Okay. **3) Have you had any fever, cough, or symptoms suggesting a lung infection (e.g., productive sputum), or is it mainly pain and shortness of breath?**

I recently had a viral infection. I don’t have a cough or fever right now, and I haven’t had productive sputum. It’s mainly the chest pain with significant shortness of breath, plus palpitations and that vague general discomfort.
Understood. **4) Are you currently having any wheezing, history of asthma/COPD, or does the shortness of breath improve with an inhaler?**
No wheezing. I don’t have asthma or COPD that I know of. I haven’t tried an inhaler yet, so I can’t say if it helps.
Got it. **5) Do you have any history of heart disease, and are you having dizziness, fainting, or sweating with the chest pain?**

I don’t have a known history of heart disease. I’ve had palpitations, and I feel unwell and achy, but I’m not having dizziness or fainting, and I’m not sure about sweating—I haven’t noticed anything like that.
Thanks. **6) When you say palpitations—do you feel a fast, irregular heartbeat (like skipping), or more like a steady fast rate?**
It feels like my heartbeat is kind of fast and maybe irregular—like it’s not totally steady, more like skipping at times.
Okay. **7) Have you noticed any rash, hives, lip/tongue swelling, or throat tightness/voice change since the viral illness?**
No, I haven’t noticed any rash, hives, or any swelling of my lips or tongue. No throat tightness or voice change either.
Thanks. **8) Does the pain change with pressing on the chest wall or moving your torso/arm (reproducible musculoskeletal pain), or is it clearly internal?**
I can’t say for sure it changes with pressing, but it feels more internal. It doesn’t clearly get better or worse with moving my torso or arm.
Understood. **9) Are you able to speak full sentences, and do you have low oxygen symptoms like bluish lips, or is it just the sensation of breathlessness?**
I can speak full sentences, but I feel very short of breath. I haven’t noticed bluish lips. It’s mostly the breathlessness sensation.
Okay. **10) Any recent surgery, pregnancy/postpartum, estrogen therapy, or known clotting disorder?**
No recent surgery, no pregnancy/postpartum, and no estrogen therapy. I don’t know of any clotting disorder.
Thanks. **11) Have you had any leg/arm weakness, numbness, or trouble swallowing, or any new neurologic symptoms?**
No, I don’t have any weakness, numbness, trouble swallowing, or any new neurologic symptoms.
Okay. **12) Do you have any history of reflux/heartburn, sour taste, or pain that’s worse after meals or when lying flat?**
I don’t have heartburn or reflux that I know of. I do feel worse when I lie down, but it’s more the shortness of breath and chest discomfort rather than sour taste or after-meal pain.
Thanks. **13) Any recent long-distance travel by car/plane, dehydration, or smoking?**
No long-distance travel. I’m not sure about dehydration, and I do smoke.
Understood. **14) Do you have any known lung conditions, or have you ever had a pneumothorax, or sudden severe one-sided chest pain before?**
No known lung conditions. I’ve never had a pneumothorax before, and I haven’t had this kind of severe one-sided chest pain previously.
[DDX] Pulmonary embolism, Acute pulmonary edema, Possible NSTEMI / STEMI, Pneumonia, Spontaneous pneumothorax
